title: Full-support bounded coherent complexes generate the module derived category
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and work in the ordinary unbounded module derived category $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $E\in D(B)$ have bounded finitely generated cohomology: there exist integers $a\le b$ such that $H^j(E)=0$ outside $[a,b]$, and each $H^j(E)$ is a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Suppose $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B_{\mathfrak p}\ne0$ for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset B$, where $B_{\mathfrak p}$ is the prime localization [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and derived tensor uses K-flat resolutions [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Let $\operatorname{Loc}_B(E)$ denote the smallest full subcategory of $D(B)$ containing $E$ and closed under isomorphisms, shifts, distinguished triangles, retracts and set-indexed coproducts. Then $B[0]\in\operatorname{Loc}_B(E)$. No finite projective or injective dimension of $E$ is assumed; $B=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent full-support localizing-generation corollary: Tags 00L0 (lemma-filter-Noetherian-module) and 00L4 (lemma-filter-primes-in-support); derived.tex Tags 09SJ (definition-generators) and 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), and more-algebra.tex Tag 09PB (remark-P-resolution). Proof by residue-field extraction and Noetherian induction is supplied in report.md; no claim that these tags state this corollary verbatim.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal L=\operatorname{Loc}_B(E)$. If $B=0$, then $B[0]=0$, which belongs to $\mathcal L$ as the empty coproduct. Henceforth treat $B\ne0$.

For every $X\in\mathcal L$, the class of $N\in D(B)$ with $X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N\in\mathcal L$ is closed under shifts, triangles, retracts and coproducts. Exactness is the derived-tensor functor theorem; for coproducts take K-flat representatives of the variable inputs. Their direct sum is K-flat, since tensor distributes over direct sums and sums of exact module sequences are exact; the total tensor also distributes over these sums. Termwise sums represent derived coproducts. This class contains $B[0]$, since $X\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B\cong X$, so free generation of $D(B)$ gives every $N$. Thus $\mathcal L$ is a tensor ideal. In particular $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\in\mathcal L$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 09PB (remark-P-resolution), applied to the inverse image of the localizing subcategory under exact tensor; agent tensor-ideal argument

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p$ and put $A=B_{\mathfrak p}$, $k=A/\mathfrak pA$. The localization definition says $A$ is local. It is Noetherian: every ideal is the extension of its contraction (write its elements as fractions), and finitely many generators of that contraction generate its extension. Exact localization identifies $H^j(E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}A)$ with $H^j(E)_{\mathfrak p}$, so the localized object is bounded with finite cohomology, and is nonzero by hypothesis. Apply local derived-tensor nonvanishing to this object and $k[0]$ in $D(A)$: both are bounded above with finite cohomology and neither is zero. Their tensor is therefore nonzero. The extension-of-scalars isomorphism in clause (2) of derived-tensor transitivity identifies its underlying $B$-object with $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}k$: in that clause use its original ring $A=B$, its $A$-algebra $C=B_{\mathfrak p}$ and its $C$-complex $K^\prime=k[0]$, giving $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}k\cong(E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B_{\mathfrak p})\otimes_{B_{\mathfrak p}}^{\mathbf L}k$. Thus $E\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}k$ is a nonzero object represented by a complex of $k$-vector spaces.

source.place: Agent residue-field extraction, using local tensor nonvanishing and the flat localization case of Tag 0BYJ

proof.text: By field-complex cohomology splitting, the $k$-complex just obtained is homotopy equivalent to its zero-differential cohomology complex, without a boundedness assumption on that tensor. Some cohomology vector space is nonzero. Choose a nonzero vector and extend it to a basis; inclusion of its line and the corresponding coordinate projection give a retract $k[-j]$ of that zero-differential complex. Restricting scalars retains the homotopy equivalence and the retract. Step 2, retract closure and shift closure yield $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[0]\in\mathcal L$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Agent residue-field extraction; vector-space complement and coordinate-retract argument

proof.text: Suppose some ideal $J\subseteq B$ has $(B/J)[0]\notin\mathcal L$, and choose a maximal such $J$. This is justified by the Noetherian condition: the union of an increasing chain of ideals is an ideal with finitely many generators, which all occur in one stage, so there is no infinite strict ascending chain. The unit ideal is not a counterexample. Take a prime filtration of the finite module $B/J$. Every prime $\mathfrak q$ occurring contains $J$, because $J$ annihilates every subquotient. If $J$ were not prime, all these inclusions would be strict; maximality would put every $(B/\mathfrak q)[0]$ in $\mathcal L$. The triangles of the filtration short exact sequences would then put $(B/J)[0]$ there. Consequently a maximal counterexample must be a prime $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00L0 (lemma-filter-Noetherian-module), maximal-counterexample proof adapted to localizing membership

proof.text: For this maximal counterexample $\mathfrak p$, let $C=\kappa(\mathfrak p)/(B/\mathfrak p)$, using the injection of the domain $B/\mathfrak p$ into its fraction field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Each finitely generated $B$-submodule $N\subseteq C$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak p$ and by some $s\notin\mathfrak p$: write its finitely many chosen generators as fractions modulo $B/\mathfrak p$ and multiply their nonzero denominators. A prime filtration of $N$ has factors $B/\mathfrak q$ with $\mathfrak q\supseteq\mathfrak p+(s)$, because this ideal annihilates each factor. Thus $\mathfrak q\supsetneq\mathfrak p$ and maximality puts every factor in $\mathcal L$. The filtration triangles give $N[0]\in\mathcal L$. The finitely generated submodules of $C$ form a small nonempty directed poset under inclusion (upper bound $N_1+N_2$), with union $C$. Closure under directed module colimits now gives $C[0]\in\mathcal L$.

source.place: Agent Noetherian induction using Tag 00L0 (lemma-filter-Noetherian-module); torsion quotient and directed union

proof.text: The short exact sequence $0\to B/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to C\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle. Its middle and last terms belong to $\mathcal L$ by steps 4 and 6; rotation and shift closure imply $(B/\mathfrak p)[0]\in\mathcal L$, contrary to the choice of $\mathfrak p$. Hence every $(B/J)[0]$ belongs to $\mathcal L$. Taking $J=0$ proves the required $B[0]\in\mathcal L$.

source.place: Agent Noetherian induction, final short exact sequence
